newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts rates 0.5 pt on bond issues- c. bank.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts rates 0.5 pt on bond issues- c. bank.

text.p: Morocco cut interest rates on short- and medium-term public Treasury bond issues by half a point to between 8.0 and 9.0 percent, an official at Bank al-Maghrib (central bank) said on Friday.

"To stimulate the money market, the monetary authorities took the decision to cut by half a point (0.50 percent) interest rates on short- and medium-term public T-bond-issues (emprunts nationaux)," the official, who declined to be named told Reuters.
Subscriptions will be open from June 30 to July 3, the official said.

The authorities reduced the interest rate on 52-week Treasury bonds to 8.0 percent. It also cut three-year T-bond issue rates to 8.5 percent and five-year Treasury bond rates to 9.0 percent, the official said.
"The move aims to encourage competition on the local market and help enterprises to raise funds on the bourse," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
Public Treasury bonds are listed on the Casablanca stock exchange.
Divided in tranches of 5,000 dirhams ($53.2) and 50,000 dirhams ($5,319), the bonds are opened to the public and all institutional operators, including foreigners, the stockbroker said.
Every three months, the authorities issue public T-bonds, and this was the third time in nine months it cut interest rates by 0.50 percent, he added.
The cuts took place after "a three-week wrestling match" between the public Treasury and commercial banks over rates on short-, medium- and long-term Treasury bills.

"For three weeks, the Treasury rejected offers of up to 1.86 billion dirhams at its weekly bill auction...But finally, accepted on Wednesday offers totalling 1.25 billion dirhams when interest rates were lowered by half a point," a finance ministry official said.
Treasury bill interest rates are "now in line with the T-bond issues," the official said.
